Returns vs. cost of living

Each bar is a month's investment return in euros; the gold line is what your life cost that month. When a bar clears the line, that month paid for itself. Months with a check-in are exact; the ones in between are estimated from your prices.

Spending control chart

An SPC individuals chart (XmR) of your monthly spending. The limits come from your own month-to-month variation, so a point outside them is unusual for you, not just a high month. Click a point to see what drove it.

Signals across your categories

Each category gets its own limits. Click a row to open its chart. Small changes under €15 aren't flagged.

CategoryAverageUpper limitLast monthStatus

Signals used: a month above the upper limit (or below the lower one), 8 months in a row on the same side of the average (the level has shifted), or 6 months moving in the same direction (a trend). The current month is still in progress, so it's only flagged if it's already above the limit.

—

Example values are only a starting point. Use the TAEG from your bank's offer.

Insurance, fuel, maintenance, condominium, IMI… Leave it at €0 for a one-off like a trip. Running costs raise your spending, so they also raise your freedom number.

Leave €0 if you don't pay rent today. Rent you'd stop paying lowers your spending, and so your freedom number.
